question: Can run 004 and 006's recipe paint the gap set, the drawer, the satchel and the rope that M2 still needs, and fit the objects and cast already approved?
why: M2 plays one complete authored episode. The path has to end at a gap the ladder really spans, the drawer has to slide out, what you give has to be keepable, and Wick needs a rope.
sameAcrossJobs: seedream5_pro, flat vivid magenta paper with a margin for cut pieces, no --seal, run 004's and 006's wording. The key and ground are full-bleed and don't get cut.
decideBy: Every piece passes make_m2.py, which exits non-zero on any problem.
The chasm measures 92-128 mm at Pip's depth, against the ladder's measured span.
The owner approves art/m2-proof.html. Final approval is in the headset.
learnEvenIfRejected: Whether a painted two-bluff layer can register against a printed chasm, and whether long thin strands survive a shared parts sheet.
reusableOutput: The gap set, drawer, satchel, rope and spans become product art. Prompts are the recipe for later sets.
capNote: Run total cap 100 credits. capCredits is reset before each invocation to objects_check.invocation_cap(spent, 100, largest). Spend for the cap is the higher of list price and the balance drop per invocation.

jobs.prompt: A wide landscape in exactly the painting style and colors of Figure 1, with no characters. The same quiet shore at gentle early dusk. The same tall old stone lighthouse stands on its far headland in the left third, dark and unlit. A strip of calm sea lies below it. In the middle distance and foreground, the sandy dune path comes from the right and stops dead at a narrow, deep chasm. The chasm runs straight down the exact center of the picture, from the foreground back to the sea, and it is exactly one quarter of the picture's width across, with ragged rock-and-sand rims. Calm dark blue-green water lies far below in it. The path carries on from the far rim toward the lighthouse. Low clumps of reeds and stones sit at the far left and far right of the foreground, dipping away to nothing toward the center. The ground beside the right rim is open and calm, for a small character to stand on. Mid-to-high values, never dark, no night. No light sources, no beams, no lit windows, no directional cast shadows. Hand-painted traditional watercolor with a fine graphite pencil outline, from a vintage natural history picture book. Soft pigment washes, visible paper grain, gentle edges. No text.

Figure 1 is the composed scene. Paint only the far rim of the chasm from Figure 1, as exactly two separate die-cut paper stage pieces, flat-on, in exactly the same painting style and colors, with a wide empty space of paper between them across the middle. On the left, a low sand-and-rock bluff with chunky grass tufts, whose right end drops steeply as a rocky cliff face. On the right, its mirror: a low bluff whose left end drops steeply as a rocky cliff face. The empty space between the two cliff faces is exactly one quarter of the image's width, centered. Neither bluff is taller than one sixth of the image's width. No sky, no sea, no lighthouse behind them: the plain paper shows directly around them. Each piece has a clean hard edge traced with a fine pencil line, and a perfectly straight flat bottom edge. Paint each piece continuously right down to its straight bottom edge, with no gaps or holes. Leave a wide margin of empty paper on all four sides, with nothing touching the edge of the image. Hand-painted traditional watercolor with a fine graphite pencil outline, from a vintage natural history picture book. Soft pigment washes, visible paper grain, gentle edges. Pale, gentle dusk values. No lit windows, no beams, no directional cast shadows. On plain flat solid vivid magenta paper, one even color. No text.
